mission: Ben considers and rejects a Jedi partner, instead calling Desh Rolan — establishing the Lie (self-reliance) through a control choice disguised as practicality
why_now: The mission requires a partner; Ben's choice of Desh over a Jedi reveals his trust architecture
conflict: Ben rationalizes choosing a non-Force-sensitive friend over a Jedi colleague as 'practical' — but it's actually about control and the danger of trusting Force-users after Jacen and Vestara
turning_point: Desh answers the comm with dry humor and agrees to the job without asking why Ben didn't call a Jedi. They both know why.
opening_hook: Ben's thumb hovers over the Jedi partner roster on his datapad, then slides past it to his personal contacts — his ship already fueled in the hangar below
closing_hook: The wrongness in the Force shifts as Ben leaves Coruscant — not diminishing but acquiring direction, like a compass needle settling
emotional_trajectory: Calculated avoidance -> familiar comfort with Desh -> unsettled recognition that the wrongness is guiding him

stakes.personal: Ben's self-deception about why he chooses isolation over Jedi partnership
stakes.interpersonal: The Ben/Desh dynamic — friendship built on shared history neither discusses
stakes.external: The wrongness has a direction — it's pulling Ben somewhere specific

setting: Jedi Temple hangar bay -> comm call to Desh -> departure from Coruscant
sensory_details: Hangar echoes; Desh's voice tinny over long-range comm; hyperspace entry — the wrongness persists through hyperspace, which it shouldn't
canon_elements_needed: Galactic Alliance Guard history, dissolution, and legacy
Non-Force-sensitive relationships with Jedi in post-war era
Coruscant to Outer Rim hyperspace travel routes and duration
Jedi Temple hangar bay layout and departure protocols
action_beats: Ben bypasses three Jedi Knight contacts on his datapad and opens his personal list
Desh's voice crackles over long-range comm — dry greeting, no questions asked
Ben's ship lifts from the Temple hangar bay and angles toward orbit
The ship punches into hyperspace; Ben's instruments flicker as the wrongness persists through the jump
promises_planted: Ben and Desh share unspoken GAG history (PP02)
Desh will matter to the climax (PP19)
notes: R01 lands at end of scene — the wrongness has a direction. This transforms Ben's departure from passive retreat to unconscious pursuit. Desh's arc starts here: lie_established — arrives as a favor, obligation not purpose. GAG backstory: Zahn-style integration — 2-3 concise sentences threaded through Ben's reaction when he registers Desh's unspoken understanding, not a standalone exposition paragraph. Give the reader enough context to feel the weight of shared history (GAG as a post-war Alliance security force whose work blurred ethical lines) without stopping the scene's forward motion. The information belongs here, but must ride on top of a beat — Ben's physical action, Desh's tone, a specific memory — rather than interrupting the scene as narrator commentary.
